title: One Day in Busan: Temple, Haeundae Beach and Korean Spa
intro: See Busan’s east coast in one day, from a seaside temple to Haeundae Beach and a Korean spa. This practical route keeps you on one side of the city, with tips for transport, rainy weather, and a long day trip from Seoul.

busan_day.note: East coast route; use a taxi to the temple

busan_overview.note: A day on Busan's east coast

segments.voice: Busan stretches a long way along the coast. Trying to cross the city all day can turn a lovely visit into a transport marathon. Here’s a simpler plan: start at a temple above the sea, spend the middle of the day at Haeundae Beach, then slow down in a Korean spa.

This route stays on the east side of Busan. You’ll travel north-east in the morning, return to Haeundae for the beach and lunch, and finish nearby in Centum City before heading back to the sea for dinner.
You don’t need to see every corner of Busan in one day. Give yourself time to enjoy each stop, and check current opening hours and transport routes before you set out.

card.title: One day on the east coast

segments.voice: If you’re arriving from Seoul, the KTX from Seoul Station to Busan Station takes about two and a half hours. But Busan Station is on the other side of the city from Haeundae. Allow about an hour to reach Haeundae by subway, changing from Line One to Line Two. For an easier start, consider staying near Haeundae the night before.
Your Seoul transit card also works on Busan’s subway and buses. Keep it handy for getting around town, but remember that the simplest way to reach Haedong Yonggungsa from Haeundae is usually a taxi.

card.title: Use your transit card
card.sub: It works on Busan subway and buses

segments.voice: For current directions, check Naver Map or KakaoMap. They can show local bus routes to the temple, too. If you take a taxi, show the driver the Korean name, 해동용궁사, or use the Kakao T app.

Check opening hours on a map app on the day, especially for SPA LAND and the Haeundae Blueline Park. The temple gets busy from mid-morning, so an early start is a good idea. Summer weekends at Haeundae are busy as well.

chapters.name: One day on Busan's east coast

segments.voice: Here’s the day in order: Haedong Yonggungsa, Haeundae Beach and its market, then SPA LAND in Centum City. Finish with dinner back in Haeundae. The temple is the outlier, so take a taxi or check the current local bus route. After that, the stops stay close to this side of the city.

card.title: A day by the sea
card.sub: Start early · stay on the east coast

segments.voice: Begin at Haedong Yonggungsa, in Gijang, north-east of Haeundae. This Buddhist temple sits on rocks above the sea, rather than tucked into the mountains like many Korean temples. That seaside setting is what makes it special. From Haeundae, a taxi takes around twenty to thirty minutes, depending on traffic. Local buses also run, so check the current route before leaving.

show.photo_query: Haedong Yonggungsa Temple on the rocky coastline in Gijang, Busan, South Korea

segments.voice: Allow about an hour to look around. Steps lead down to the main hall, so take your time. This is an active place of worship: keep your voice low and be considerate when taking photos. Going early also helps you avoid the busier mid-morning period. If you’d rather wake up closer to the temple, the Osiria area has resorts and an outlet mall, including Ananti at Busan Cove.

card.title: A quiet start helps
card.sub: Allow about an hour at the temple

segments.voice: Next, return to Haeundae Beach. It’s Busan’s best-known beach, and a good place to walk on the sand or along the promenade. On a summer weekend, expect it to be busy. Starting early at the temple lets you keep the beach for later in the morning, rather than arriving at the busiest part of the day.

show.photo_query: Haeundae Beach and promenade in Busan, South Korea

segments.voice: For lunch, head into the streets behind the beach. Haeundae Traditional Market is a short walk from the sand and makes an easy stop for snacks. Look for familiar street-food favourites like fish cakes and tteokbokki. You can keep lunch casual here, then leave room in the afternoon for a longer, slower break.

show.photo_query: Haeundae Traditional Market street food stalls in Busan, South Korea

segments.voice: If you have extra time, consider the Haeundae Blueline Park. Its beach train and small sky capsules follow the old coastal railway between Mipo, near the end of Haeundae Beach, and Cheongsapo. This is an optional add-on, not a must for a full day. Tickets for the sky capsules can sell out at busy times, so book ahead in summer and on weekends.

show.photo_query: Haeundae Blueline Park sky capsule on the coastal railway in Busan, South Korea

segments.voice: In the afternoon, take Line Two one stop from Haeundae to Centum City. SPA LAND is inside Shinsegae Centum City department store. It has hot-spring baths and themed rest rooms, and it offers a comfortable introduction to Korean bathhouse culture. Check current details before you go. If the weather turns, the same building also gives you an indoor shopping option.

show.photo_query: SPA LAND Centum City hot spring bathhouse in Busan, South Korea

segments.voice: Return to Haeundae for dinner. Ribs of Legend Haeundae is close to the beach and serves Korean grilled ribs. After dinner, keep it simple with a walk along the beach at night. Or, if you’d like to see another stretch of coast, take a short taxi ride to Gwangalli Beach, where Gwangan Bridge is lit up after dark.

show.photo_query: Korean grilled ribs at Ribs of Legend Haeundae in Busan, South Korea

segments.voice: The main transport decision is how to get to the temple. A taxi from Haeundae takes around twenty to thirty minutes, depending on traffic, and is the easiest option. Local buses also go there, but check Naver Map or KakaoMap for the current route. Later, the subway makes the Haeundae-to-Centum City leg straightforward: it’s one stop on Line Two. Your transit card works on Busan buses and subway, just as it does in Seoul.

card.title: Keep travel simple
card.sub: Taxi to the temple · Line Two to Centum City

segments.voice: Three easy mistakes to avoid: trying to cross all of Busan in one day, leaving the temple until later, and assuming you can get a sky-capsule ticket whenever you arrive.

list.heading: Keep the day manageable
items: Stay on one side of Busan
Book sky capsules ahead at busy times
Check hours and routes on the day

segments.voice: Busan is spread out, so focus on the east coast instead of adding distant sights. Going early helps with the temple’s mid-morning crowds, and it leaves the beach for later in the morning. If you want the Blueline Park sky capsules, plan ahead for summer and weekends, when tickets can sell out. And don’t rely on old transport or opening-hour information: check a map app on the day, especially for the temple route and the spa.

Can you visit Busan as a day trip from Seoul? Yes, the KTX makes it possible, and the journey from Seoul Station to Busan Station takes about two and a half hours. But add about an hour to reach Haeundae from Busan Station by subway, changing from Line One to Line Two. It makes for a long day. Staying at least one night, ideally near Haeundae, gives you more time.

card.title: A day trip is possible
card.sub: But staying overnight gives you more time

segments.voice: What’s the easiest way to reach Haedong Yonggungsa? Take a taxi from Haeundae; allow around twenty to thirty minutes, depending on traffic. Local buses also run. Check Naver Map or KakaoMap for the current route, or show a taxi driver the Korean name, 해동용궁사.

show.photo_query: Taxi outside Haedong Yonggungsa Temple in Busan, South Korea

segments.voice: Does this plan work on a rainy day? Partly. The temple and beach are outdoors, so those stops may be less comfortable in poor weather. The spa and Shinsegae Centum City are indoors, so you can stretch out that part of the afternoon if the weather is bad.

show.photo_query: SPA LAND Centum City interior rest area in Busan, South Korea

segments.voice: The plan is simple: start early at Haedong Yonggungsa, return to Haeundae for the beach and market lunch, then take Line Two to SPA LAND in Centum City. Come back for grilled ribs and a seaside walk. Add the Blueline Park only if you have time, and consider Gwangalli for the night view.
